thread:
sarah: Hey support — customer 'AcmeMaps' hitting intermittent 401s after we rotated their svc key this morning. They see failures only through their edge proxy, direct requests to our hosted endpoint succeed. Request IDs they pasted: r_2b9f1c, r_2b9f2d. Can someone help gather repro steps?

mike: Can you drop the exact curl they used and the raw response body (headers + body)?

sarah: Pasting the curl they ran (sanitized keys):

```
curl -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer SVCKEY_REDACTED" \
  -H "X-Org-ID: acme-999" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"input":"status"}'
```

Their intermittent success pattern: runs 10 requests in a loop, ~7 succeed (200) and ~3 return 401 JSON: `{"error":"unauthorized","message":"signature mismatch","request_id":"r_2b9f1c"}`

ingrid: That smells like header canonicalization or a proxy rewriting Authorization. If their proxy is caching servicekey-to-org mapping and a recent rotation happened, proxy might be sending an old key on some connections. Ask them to capture -v and full response headers. Also ask for the proxy config that forwards headers.

sarah: They sent a small server log excerpt (redacted):
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:01.432Z] req=r_2b9f1c auth=svc acct=acme-999 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=401 err="signature mismatch" remote=10.4.12.8
[2026-03-15T09:12:01.433Z] req=r_2b9f1d auth=svc acct=acme-999 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=200 latency_ms=23 remote=10.4.12.8
[2026-03-15T09:12:02.110Z] req=r_2b9f2d auth=svc acct=acme-999 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=401 err="signature mismatch" remote=10.4.12.9
```

mike: Ok. Two hypotheses: 1) upstream proxy sometimes strips or rewrites Authorization header on keepalive reuse, 2) proxy is multiplexing connections with a per-connection cached credential (old key) and not picking up rotated key. Let's ask customer to run a deterministic repro and capture wire bytes. Provide reproducible steps they can run: 1) run curl loop with unique id header, 2) capture tcpdump on client-facing interface, 3) include -v output + server request ids.

sarah: Suggested repro command for them to run locally against their proxy (replace interface and filename):
```
for i in {1..20}; do \
  curl -s -w "\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code} RID:%{header_request_id}"\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer SVCKEY_REDACTED" -H "X-Org-ID: acme-999" -H "X-Debug-Tag: looptest-$i" -o /tmp/out.$i \
  https://proxy.acme.internal/rdw-proxy/v1/generate; \
done
# On their proxy host (linux): sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/proxy-looptest.pcap port 443 & sleep 30; kill $!
```
(we asked them to include the pcap and the /tmp/out.* files)

ingrid: Also ask them to add this header to the curl so we can track how their proxy forwards the incoming Authorization: `-H "X-Original-Authorization: $(printf '%s' "Bearer SVCKEY_REDACTED")"` — if X-Original-Authorization differs from final request we received, proxy rewrites.

ryan-oncall: Another thing: some frontend proxies drop `Authorization` when TLS terminates and then re-issues requests to backend using an internal service identity. If the proxy is not mapping org/project correctly, the backend will see a mismatch and reject. Request them to share proxy config snippet, especially `proxy_set_header Authorization` lines (nginx) or forwarding rules (envoy).

sarah: Customer shared a tiny nginx snippet they use: 
```
location /rdw-proxy/ {
  proxy_pass https://api.redwood.ai/;
  proxy_set_header Host $host;
  proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
  # suspect line below often omitted in their older configs:
  # proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;
}
```
They commented out the Authorization forward. That would explain the 401s — but weird that some requests succeed. Could be that keepalive reuses an existing upstream connection that still had Authorization set from a previous request. When the proxy accidentally forwards Authorization for some upstream connections (leftover header), backend accepts; other connections lack it -> 401.

mike: Good find. Next steps for customer (actionable):
1) Re-enable `proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;` in their nginx (or equivalent in envoy).
2) Re-run the curl loop with tcpdump and -v. Upload the pcap and one of the failing `out.*` files and note the failing RID.
3) If they cannot change config immediately, ask them to force non-keepalive upstream to avoid header bleed: add `proxy_set_header Connection "close";` as a temporary test.

support-bot: Created internal support case #SUP-2026-0042 and presigned S3 upload: s3://redwood-debug/sup-2026-0042/acmemaps/ (expires in 72h). Please upload pcap + out files and paste the failing request_id(s) in the thread.

sarah: I'll email the customer the steps and the presigned link. I'll ask them to include the most recent failing request_id. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

mike: Once we get the pcap and RID, we'll correlate with our ingress traces and confirm if the backend saw missing Authorization header then close the loop. If it's proxy config we can provide a short patch to their infra.

sarah: Update will follow when they upload.
